answer: A collateralized endorsement protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to stake slashing bonds for new entrants. To anchor each identity in a branching cedar trust graph, sponsors lock funds in a saffron escrow pool that burns collateral if peers misbehave. An attacker must commit scarce, liquid capital per simulated agent. However, this reliance on bonded trust favors entrenched cartels, creating barriers for legitimate newcomers.
